T100000130327.name: Australia Pacific LNG Terminal
hw: 7x gas turbine generators (Bechtel-constructed), each ~15 MW peak, combined ~105 MW, powering the two LNG processing trains on Curtis Island.
notes: APLNG's Curtis Island facility runs 7 on-site gas turbine generators (~15 MW each, ~105 MW combined) that generate the electrical power to operate the two LNG trains, fueled by a portion of the facility's own feed gas. This is a dedicated on-site generating plant carrying normal site load, not a mechanical-drive/shaft-power arrangement.

T100000130330.name: Crib Point FSRU Terminal
hw: FSRU-mounted dual fuel engines plus three gas-fired boilers (model/rating not disclosed in the source found); per AGL/APA's own EES risk assessment (Chapter 23, Climate Change Adaptation) the FSRU is 'electrically isolated from Jetty and generates its own power' as its normal operating arrangement, not a contingency-only backup.
notes: AGL/APA's Crib Point Gas Import Jetty (a moored FSRU plus a 56 km pipeline to the Pakenham transmission network in Victoria) underwent a full Environment Effects Statement before being rejected by the Victorian Government in March 2021. The EES itself (quoted in a public submission) states the FSRU is 'electrically isolated from Jetty and generates its own power' via onboard dual fuel engines/boilers documented to run on gas — i.e. the vessel is designed to be self-sufficient for its own electricity, not shore-powered, consistent with the SOP's FSRU-onboard-generation convention. This is a design-stage finding (project was rejected in 2021 before construction), which still counts under the 'as-designed captive power on an unbuilt facility' rule.

T100000130331.name: Darwin LNG Terminal
hw: On-site power-generation gas turbines fueled by facility fuel gas (count/individual rating undisclosed in the source found); Santos (operator) describes a 2019 battery-integration project layered onto these 'existing power generation turbines.'
notes: Darwin LNG (Wickham Point, NT; operated by Santos) runs on-site gas-fired power generation turbines that supply the plant's electrical load; a 2019 battery project was added to run them more efficiently and cut fuel-gas consumption and emissions. This replaces the previously-staged, unrelated generic-turbine-lecture reference with a primary operator source. [REF DROP declared (QC gate): https://turbolab.tamu.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/Lecture-08.pdf — generic gas-turbine lecture PDF; does not mention Darwin LNG]

T100000130333.name: Gladstone LNG Terminal
hw: 6× gas turbine generators on Curtis Island, ~12 MW each (~72 MW aggregate), providing the plant's permanent electrical power supply
notes: Santos GLNG's Curtis Island plant runs on 6 on-site gas turbine generators (~12 MW each, ~72 MW total) that supply permanent electrical power to the LNG plant, running all heavy electrical equipment including compressors and pumps. This confirms and updates GEM's existing True/ref.

T100000130334.name: Gorgon LNG Terminal
hw: 5× gas turbine generators on Barrow Island, generating up to 584 MW at full output, providing power to the Gorgon LNG/domestic-gas processing operation
notes: Chevron's Gorgon LNG/domestic gas complex on Barrow Island is powered by 5 on-site gas turbine generators capable of generating up to 584 MW — 'almost as much as the Kwinana power station which supplies much of greater Perth' — described by Chevron Australia's managing director as a critical element of the Barrow Island processing operation's commissioning. This confirms and updates GEM's existing True/ref.

T100000130335.name: Ichthys FLNG Terminal
hw: On-site combined cycle power plant at the Bladin Point onshore LNG processing facility, providing electricity to the two LNG trains, LPG/condensate plants, and site utilities (turbine count/model/MW not disclosed in the source found)
notes: INPEX's own project page states that Ichthys LNG's onshore processing facilities at Bladin Point include, alongside the two LNG trains and LPG/condensate plants, 'a combined cycle power plant' — i.e., a dedicated on-site gas-turbine generating plant, not a grid connection. MW capacity is not disclosed in this source.

T100000130337.name: North West Shelf LNG Terminal
hw: Aero-derivative gas turbine generators supply on-site electricity at the Karratha Gas Plant (North West Shelf Venture, Woodside-operated); the Train 4 expansion (online 2004) added further "high-efficiency gas turbine (aero-derivative) generators to augment existing power generation" (confirming on-site generation predates Train 4 too), and an independent trade-news report of a 2026 cyclone shutdown confirms the plant's "gas turbine power generators" as an operating asset class distinct from the LNG trains and domestic gas plant ("the North West Shelf (NWS) project's four liquefied natural gas (LNG) trains, gas turbine power generators and the domestic gas plant are all down"). Turbine model/count/individual MW not itemized in either source.
notes: The Karratha Gas Plant (North West Shelf Venture, Woodside-operated) generates its own electricity on-site via aero-derivative gas turbine generators. Upgraded from the primary pass's single-source yellow: a second, genuinely independent Australian trade-energy outlet (Boiling Cold, reporting a 2026 cyclone shutdown) separately confirms "gas turbine power generators" as a distinct, named operating asset at the site — not a mirror of the GlobalData/offshore-technology.com profile used in the primary pass.

T100000130338.name: Pluto LNG Terminal
hw: A dedicated "gas-fired power generation facility" is listed among Pluto LNG's on-site infrastructure (alongside its BOG compressor, acid gas recovery and fractionation units); separately, Woodside's own Q2 2026 quarterly report (as quoted by Energy Aspects' satellite-commissioning analysis) states that during Train 2 commissioning "the gas turbine generator completed synchronisation with the Pluto power grid" — confirming a generator supplying an on-site electrical grid at Pluto, not merely a design-stage claim. Turbine model/count/individual MW not itemized in either source.
notes: Pluto LNG (Woodside-operated, Karratha, Burrup Peninsula) has on-site gas-fired power generation: a "gas-fired power generation facility" is documented as part of the plant's infrastructure, and Woodside's own Q2 2026 report (quoted independently by Energy Aspects) confirms a "gas turbine generator" synchronised to the on-site "Pluto power grid" during Train 2 commissioning. Two independent sources (a GlobalData/nsenergybusiness project profile and Energy Aspects, an independent energy research firm citing Woodside's own report) confirm the finding — upgraded from the primary pass's INSUFFICIENT (which was blocked purely by a citation-tooling gap, not doubt about the underlying fact).

T100000130339.name: Prelude FLNG Terminal
hw: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries supplied "three compressor trains along with power generation system" for the facility (Jan 2011 contract award); General Electric independently confirms (its own press release) it supplied "two steam turbine-driven compressors" for Prelude, describing its scope as covering "the steam turbines and compressors" with minimized casings to reduce weight/footprint; Kawasaki Heavy Industries supplied seven boiler units that raise the steam for GE's turbines. Turbine models and MW ratings for the MHI power-generation system are not itemized in either source.
notes: Prelude FLNG (Shell-operated, moored offshore, world's largest FLNG) has a dedicated on-site power generation system (Mitsubishi Heavy Industries-supplied, alongside its three compressor trains) plus General Electric steam-turbine-driven compressors fed by steam from seven Kawasaki-supplied boiler units. Upgraded from the primary pass's single-source yellow: GE's own press release (vendor-primary, confirming its steam-turbine/compressor scope of supply for Prelude in its own words) independently corroborates the nsenergybusiness trade profile.

T100000130340.name: Queensland Curtis LNG Terminal
hw: 15 GE aeroderivative gas turbines driving 28 centrifugal compressors via gearboxes, plus generators, installed as part of QCLNG's Curtis Island LNG facility (GE's supply/service scope, per GE's own press release) — models/individual ratings not broken out in the source.
notes: QCLNG's Curtis Island facility runs 15 GE aeroderivative gas turbines driving 28 centrifugal compressors via gearboxes plus on-site generators, per GE's own press release stating its gas turbines, compressors and generators 'are integral parts of the QCLNG facility.' This confirms both mechanical-drive compression and on-site electricity generation. The current GEM ref (a Bechtel construction-progress YouTube video) does not itself document captive power and is not a useful citation for this value. [REF DROP declared (QC gate): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mFB3arwpSKY&t=8s — Bechtel construction video; no captive-power content]

T100000130343.name: Tassie Shoal LNG Terminal
hw: LM6000 aero-derivative gas turbine drivers (mechanical-drive, for refrigeration compression) plus a dedicated on-site 'Power Generation' process module supplying electric-driven compressors, per the completed Pre-FEED design (WorleyParsons/Arup, with APCI liquefaction-technology input) — turbine count/MW rating not disclosed.
notes: The Tassie Shoal LNG Project (TSLNG) design — a fixed, sea-floor-mounted 3.0 MTA LNG plant (expandable to 4.0 MTA) proposed for stranded Bonaparte Basin/Timor Sea gas — specifies 'LM6000 Aero-derivative gas turbine drivers' as a Key Project Metric alongside 'Electric drives,' with the process-flow diagram in the developer's own flyer labeling a dedicated 'Power Generation' block among the plant's process modules. As an as-designed Pre-FEED feature on a shelved, never-built project, this counts as captive gas power under the design-basis rule (both mechanical-drive turbines and a dedicated power-generation module feeding the electric drives).

T100000130344.name: Wheatstone LNG Terminal
hw: 12x GE LM6000PF aero-derivative gas turbines (6 per LNG train, 2 trains) in mechanical-drive service, driving the ConocoPhillips Optimized Cascade refrigeration compressors — the first industrial application of the LM6000PF for mechanical drive; Train 2 later upgraded to LM6000PF+.
notes: Wheatstone's two-train LNG facility (Ashburton North Strategic Industrial Area, WA) uses 12 GE LM6000PF aero-derivative gas turbines (6 per train) purely in mechanical-drive service to drive the refrigeration compressor strings directly — no electricity is generated by these units. This is documented directly by Chevron's own engineers in a 2019 IGU/LNG2019 conference technical paper, which is sufficient alone (operator technical paper) for a green verdict. [REF DROP declared (QC gate): https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/chevron-australia-starts-repair-work-wheatstone-platform-says-spokesperson-2024-06-13/ — platform-repair news story; Wayback 20240613101004 full text contains no turbine/generator/power content]

T100000130303.name: Papua LNG Terminal
hw: On-site combined-cycle gas-fired power plant(s) generating all of the project's electricity; liquefaction trains use electric-drive compressors (not gas-turbine mechanical drive) — no generator count/MW disclosed on the operator's page.
notes: Papua LNG's own developer site states the project is designed for zero Scope 2 emissions because it does not import electricity: 'energy required for operations will be generated within the project's own facilities' via 'combined cycle power plants.' The new liquefaction trains use electric drives rather than gas-turbine mechanical drive, so all captive generation here is electric power generation, none of it mechanical shaft-drive.

T100000130304.name: Papua New Guinea LNG Terminal
hw: Multiple aero-derivative gas turbine generators (one held in standby) providing primary electrical power (base load 44,000 kW / 44.267 MW, sized up to 59,760 kW with 20% growth + 15% contingency allowance) PLUS separate aero-derivative gas turbines shaft-driving the refrigerant/liquefaction compressors (mechanical drive, no electricity generated); diesel-engine generators are provided separately for essential/black-start power only (non-gas, out of scope).
notes: PNG LNG's Environmental Impact Statement (Chapter 4, a primary regulatory filing) documents a fully self-contained power system: gas turbine generators (one in standby) meet an estimated 44,000 kW base electrical load (Table 4.1: LNG trains 20,060 kW + storage 10,847 kW + utilities 5,782 kW + offsites 3,753 kW + camps 3,825 kW = 44,267 kW total, growing to 59,760 kW with margins), all fuelled by the plant's own high-pressure fuel gas system. Separately, aero-derivative gas turbines mechanically drive the refrigerant compressors (shaft power, not generation) — the base case selected specifically over heavier frame-turbine technology for lower emissions. Diesel-engine generators exist only for black-start/essential backup and are excluded (non-gas).
